strategy.summary: Reproduce UECMResults.resid returning endog-based residuals instead of model._y-based residuals by building statsmodels at the buggy commit 0a347973915a with the PR test added, then running test_uecm_resid in the ARDL test module. The test fails on the buggy revision and passes on the fixed one.

system_packages: C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) needed to build statsmodels Cython extensions
pinned_because: No dependency constraint is documented (documented_constraint null) and no era ceiling is given, so no version is pinned by evidence. Relying on the unbounded era-inferred choice: use the current numpy, scipy and pandas that install cleanly on the chosen Python, and state this choice explicitly.

The nightly wheel from the scientific-python-nightly-wheels index is not used for reproduction, because it may not correspond to the exact buggy commit; a source build at 0a347973915a is needed to guarantee the buggy resid property is present.

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/tsa/ardl/tests/test_ardl.py::test_uecm_resid, which fits UECM(dane_data.lrm, 3, dane_data[[lry, ibo, ide]], {lry: 1, ibo: 3, ide: 2}) and asserts np.testing.assert_allclose(res.resid, res.model._y - res.fittedvalues)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 0a347973915a with the test added, test_uecm_resid fails, either as an assert_allclose mismatch or as a shape-mismatch error, because resid is endog minus fittedvalues and not model._y minus fittedvalues. On the fixed revision (the PR merge that overrides resid in UECMResults to compute model._y - fittedvalues), the same test passes. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "from statsmodels.tsa.ardl.tests.test_ardl import dane_data; from statsmodels.tsa.ardl import UECM; r=UECM(dane_data.lrm,3,dane_data[['lry','ibo','ide']],{'lry':1,'ibo':3,'ide':2}).fit(); print(r.resid.shape, r.model._y.shape, r.model.endog.shape)"
risks: Architecture and platform: the defect is a plain Python-level property override and should not depend on CPU architecture, BLAS, threading or sanitisers, so it should reproduce on any x86_64 or arm64 Linux, macOS or Windows host that can build statsmodels.
The buggy commit must be built from source; running the nightly wheel or a conda package may fall on a different revision where resid is already fixed, giving a false pass.

The failure mode on buggy code may be a shape mismatch rather than a value mismatch, depending on whether model.endog and model._y have the same length for UECM. Either outcome counts as failing, but the failure message will differ from a numerical difference.

The test uses numpy assert_allclose at its default tolerance (rtol 1e-7, atol 0). Passing on the fixed revision relies on the fixed expression being algebraically identical to the asserted one, which should hold exactly.
The issue notes the fix may not be backported to the stable release, so the branch must be main at or after the PR merge for the fixed run, and the buggy commit for the failing run.
The test references dane_data from the same test module; if the dataset file is missing or the module imports fail, the test errors on both revisions, which does not show a transition.

oracle.tolerance: numpy default for assert_allclose: rtol=1e-7, atol=0
oracle.reference_source: test_uecm_resid in the PR 9812 test diff, comparing res.resid to res.model._y - res.fittedvalues
oracle.why: The fixed resid property is defined as model._y minus fittedvalues, so the asserted expression matches it up to floating-point identity; the tolerance only guards against rounding.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 0a347973915a, UECMResults.resid is inherited as endog minus fittedvalues, using model.endog (levels) rather than model._y (differenced dependent variable). assert_allclose therefore either raises a shape-mismatch error or reports a large mismatch between res.resid and res.model._y - res.fittedvalues, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, UECMResults overrides resid to return model._y - fittedvalues, which is identical to the asserted right-hand side, so assert_allclose passes and test_uecm_resid is green.
